data.title: Stack Trace
data.tagline: The position list printed when a program fails, ordered from the failure point back to the entry
data.learningOutcome: You can find a frame from your own file near the top of an error stack and use it as a location clue.
data.description: In JavaScript and Node.js, a stack trace commonly lists the frame nearest the throw near the top, followed by its callers. Start near the top and find a frame in your own file; it gives a location clue, not proof of the root cause.

learning.assumes: You have seen error text in a terminal or an AI mentioning a failing line.
learning.outcome: You can find a frame from your own file near the top of an error stack and use it as a location clue.

distinctions.label: Server logs
distinctions.explanation: Logs record what happened over time, keeping many entries. A stack trace describes only the call positions at the moment of failure, not the full request history.

distinctions.label: On-page error text
distinctions.explanation: The message a user sees is a sentence the product writes. A stack trace is raw position output from inside the program, usually visible only in a terminal, logs, or an AI investigation.

explanation.title: The frame near the throw is usually near the top
explanation.text: The frame nearest the throw is usually near the top, followed by its callers; a runtime or third-party frame may appear first.

explanation.title: Look for your own files only
explanation.text: The trace can mix in runtime and third-party library internals. Only frames from your own files correspond to code you wrote and can be a starting point for a fix.

explanation.title: The error type points at a value
explanation.text: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined means code tried to read a property from undefined; check the failing line and actual data to find which value was undefined.

data.boundary: A stack trace says where it failed, not why. The same error can come from empty data, a wrong argument, or an upstream change, so the cause still needs code and real data to confirm.

lessonPractice.title: Running the project reports TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined. The top frame is a Node internal file, and the middle shows at loadRows (save.js:24:21). What should happen next?

options.label: Find the frame in your own file, save.js:24, and read that line first
options.feedback: The top frame can be Node or a third-party library internals. A frame in your own file corresponds to code you wrote and is where investigation starts.

options.label: Read only the topmost line because errors always start there
options.feedback: The topmost frame is just the function running when it failed; it can belong to the runtime and have nothing to do with your code.

options.label: Send the whole error to AI without judging anything
options.feedback: Sending the full trace to AI is fine, but identifying your own file's frame first confirms AI fixes the right location.

data.agentPrompt: Running node save.js reports a TypeError, and the stack points to my loadRows (save.js:24:21). Start near that frame, then trace its caller and input data to find where undefined first appears; rerun after the fix and verify the result.
